Yes. bottom-right fills BR and TL. So consistent.

Now, is there any issue with the verifier detecting frame bounds? It finds all 5s. Our frame is 6x6 border, so rows 2-7, cols 2-7. rmin=2, rmax=7, cmin=2, cmax=7. Good. Dots at (1,1), etc. The verifier checks input_grid[rmin-1, cmin-1] etc. For example A, top_left at (1,1)=1. top_right at (1,8)=4. bottom_left at (8,1)=0, bottom_right at (8,8)=0. So only top_left and top_right. Good.

What about row8 col1 in Example A? It's 0, so bottom_left not detected. Good.

All good.

Should we show more than 4? The number of pairs recorded. More examples might help but could also be redundant. 4 is sufficient to cover all adjacent pairs. Maybe include a fifth with different colors to show that colors can be any. But 4 already have different colors. Could include an example where dots are at top-left and bottom-right? I'm still torn. Let's read task description carefully: "Outside the frame, exactly two colored dots appear at positions adjacent to the frame's corners — each dot sits one cell diagonally outward from a corner of the grey frame." It doesn't say distinct corners? It says "at positions adjacent to the frame's corners" and later "each positioned one cell diagonally from a distinct corner of the frame." Yes distinct. But distinct could include opposite. "For each colored dot, identify which corner of the frame it is nearest to. That dot's color fills the 2×2 quadrant on the interior side of that corner, AND the diagonally opposite 2×2 quadrant. The other dot's color fills the remaining two quadrants." If dots are opposite, the remaining two quadrants are not filled by either dot's rule? Actually if top-left and bottom-right, top-left fills TL and BR. bottom-right fills BR and TL. The remaining two quadrants (TR, BL) are not filled by top-left nor bottom-right. So "the other dot's color fills the remaining two quadrants" is false. Therefore the rule implicitly assumes dots are on adjacent corners. The generator likely ensures that. So skip opposite.

What about dots on same side but one color same? Not relevant.

Thus 4 examples.
